name: AZ-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Grijalva with large fundraising advantage
Republican challenger underfunded with minimal cash
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to the incumbent: a D+13 district, Grijalva's $2.3 million raised against Butierez's $224 thousand, and Polymarket pricing her at 95% all align on a comfortable Democratic margin in the low twenties.
model.watch: Any late polling showing an unusually favorable Republican environment or a surge of outside spending against Grijalva would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Adelita Grijalva, the Democratic incumbent in this heavily Democratic southern Arizona district, seeks a full term after winning the seat. The district's D+13 partisan lean gives her a substantial structural advantage, and her incumbency adds a further cushion.

The money gap is stark: Grijalva has raised roughly $2.3 million and holds over $400 thousand on hand, while Republican Daniel Butierez has raised about $224 thousand with under $12 thousand remaining and no outside support. Prediction markets put her chances around 95%. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on these fundamentals, all of which point to a safe Democratic hold.
